general_information: Common colds are typically self-limiting viral upper respiratory infections.
Symptoms usually peak within 2 to 3 days and gradually resolve within 7 to 10 days.
self_care: Get adequate rest and sleep to support immune function.
Drink plenty of fluids such as warm water, clear broths, and herbal teas.
Use warm saline gargles for throat discomfort.
Consider steam inhalation to ease nasal congestion.
Wash hands frequently with soap and water to prevent viral transmission.
warning_signs: Difficulty breathing or persistent chest discomfort
High fever persisting beyond 3 days
Inability to swallow liquids or severe throat swelling
Sudden worsening after initial improvement
when_to_seek_care: Symptoms persist without improvement beyond 10 days
Severe earache or persistent sinus pain develops
Patient has compromised immunity or chronic respiratory illness
entries.source: World Health Organization (WHO) & MoHFW Clinical Guidance

general_information: Fever is a natural physiological defense mechanism against infection.
An isolated mild elevation in temperature without alarming symptoms is common in brief viral illnesses.
self_care: Rest in a comfortably cool, well-ventilated room with lightweight clothing.
Maintain high oral fluid intake to prevent fever-induced dehydration.
Apply lukewarm sponge baths to forehead and body if feeling overheated (never use cold ice water).
Monitor body temperature regularly using a clean digital thermometer.
warning_signs: Fever accompanied by a stiff neck, confusion, or extreme lethargy
Fever with a new unexplained skin rash (petechiae or purple spots)
Fever exceeding 3 days without identifiable source
Rapid breathing or grunting in young infants
when_to_seek_care: Any fever in an infant under 3 months requires immediate medical evaluation
Fever lasting longer than 3 days in children or adults
Patient unable to keep oral fluids down due to vomiting
entries.source: WHO Integrated Management of Childhood Illness (IMCI) & MoHFW

general_information: Acute cough is a protective reflex clearing irritants and mucus from the airways.
Most viral coughs resolve naturally over 2 to 3 weeks.
self_care: Keep the throat hydrated with warm water, lemon water, or warm soups.
Use warm steam inhalation to loosen airway secretions.
Elevate head while sleeping if night coughing disturbs rest.
Avoid exposure to active or passive cigarette smoke, dust, and harsh fumes.
warning_signs: Coughing up blood or rust-colored sputum
Shortness of breath, wheezing, or stridor (high-pitched breathing noise)
Severe sharp chest pain when breathing in
Cough persisting longer than 3 to 4 weeks
when_to_seek_care: Cough lasting more than 2 weeks without improvement
Accompanied by unexplained night sweats or weight loss
Pre-existing asthma, COPD, or cardiac conditions
entries.source: National Health Portal of India (MoHFW) & WHO Respiratory Guidelines

general_information: Mild tension headaches are frequently linked to stress, dehydration, eye strain, or sleep deprivation.
self_care: Rest in a quiet, dimly lit, well-ventilated room.
Drink a large glass of water to rule out dehydration as a trigger.
Apply a cool or warm cloth to forehead or back of neck.
Take breaks from digital computer/phone screens and practice gentle neck stretches.
warning_signs: Sudden, explosive severe headache ('worst headache of life' or thunderclap headache)
Headache accompanied by fever, neck stiffness, or confusion
Headache following recent head trauma or injury
Accompanied by focal neurological symptoms: weakness, numbness, or vision loss
when_to_seek_care: Headache frequency or severity steadily escalates over days
Persistent headache in individuals aged over 50 with new onset
Accompanied by persistent nausea and vomiting
entries.source: WHO Fact Sheet on Headache Disorders & MoHFW

general_information: Acute diarrhea is the passage of three or more loose or watery stools per day.
The primary risk of acute diarrhea and vomiting is fluid loss and dehydration.
self_care: Prepare and sip WHO-formulated Oral Rehydration Salts (ORS) solution regularly according to package directions.
Drink clean boiled water, coconut water, rice water, or light broths.
Continue light, easily digestible foods like bananas, rice, and khichdi.
Do not withhold food or fluids.
Wash hands thoroughly with soap after using the toilet and before preparing food.
warning_signs: Signs of severe dehydration: sunken eyes, extreme thirst, no urine for >8 hours, dry mouth, lethargy
Presence of visible red blood or black tarry substance in stool
Continuous high fever or intractable vomiting preventing oral fluid retention
Diarrhea persisting for more than 48 hours without slowing down
when_to_seek_care: Infants or young children showing decreased alertness or sunken soft spot (fontanelle)
Inability to tolerate even small sips of ORS fluid
Elderly individuals or those with kidney or cardiac disease
entries.source: WHO Guidelines on Diarrhoeal Disease & MoHFW Child Health Division

general_information: Mild generalized symptoms often indicate physiological recovery needs or mild viral reactivity.
Active monitoring and hydration form the foundation of non-pharmacological self-care.
self_care: Prioritize 7-8 hours of quality sleep to aid recovery.
Maintain balanced nutritional intake with wholesome, home-cooked foods.
Ensure consistent hydration throughout the day.
Avoid smoking, alcohol, and excessive caffeine during recovery.
warning_signs: Unexplained rapid weight loss or severe night sweats
Sudden onset of severe localized pain
Changes in consciousness, speech, or mobility
when_to_seek_care: Symptoms worsen or fail to show gradual improvement over 3 to 5 days
Presence of pre-existing uncontrolled chronic illnesses
entries.source: World Health Organization Public Health Guidance
